title: Lake radius of gyration: two-dimensional territory independent of shoreline fractality
status: Specified and committed BEFORE the lake polygons were obtained. The data host was not reachable from the registering environment; experiments/run_lake_gyration.py is ready to run where it is. The prediction was first committed in docs/resource-catalogue.md (commit e4bf526).
prior_exposure: The registrant knows published lake-AREA exponents (Cael and Seekell 2016 and corrigendum: tau = 2.14 above 0.46 km^2). No distribution of lake radii of gyration has been read.
question: Do lakes tile the land surface as a two-dimensional territory, so that the count per logarithmic class of linear size falls as L^-2 whatever the fractal dimension of their area?

H_territory.why: Territory rule with support dimension d_s = 2 and linear size R (D_k = 1): survival exponent zeta_R = 2, density exponent 3. Independent of the area-size dimension D, because the territory is counted, not the water area.

H_area_inherited.why: If the area distribution were primary, zeta_R would equal the fitted area exponent times the fitted area-radius dimension D (from log A on log R), e.g. 1.14 x 2 = 2.28 for compact lakes. This is an identity check that the territory hypothesis must also satisfy, with zeta_A = 2/D.

data.source: HydroLAKES v1.0 polygons (Messager et al. 2016, Nature Communications 7, 13603; CC BY 4.0), https://www.hydrosheds.org/products/hydrolakes, shapefile HydroLAKES_polys_v10_shp.zip, about 1.43 million lakes of at least 10 ha.
data.variable: Radius of gyration R of each polygon (outer ring, area-weighted, holes ignored), computed after projecting to an equal-area projection (EPSG:6933).

estimator.range: Fixed in advance: lakes with area between 1 km^2 and 1,000 km^2, to stay above the 10 ha mapping limit and below the few largest lakes; R bounds are taken as the 0.5% and 99.5% quantiles of R within that area range.
estimator.model: Truncated (bounded) power law for R on [R_lo, R_hi], maximum likelihood (src/gof.fit_powerlaw); zeta_R = alpha - 1.
estimator.uncertainty: Percentile 95% interval from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of lakes, and a spatial-block bootstrap by HydroBASINS level-3 region if the basin field is present.
estimator.dimension_D: Ordinary least squares slope of log A on log R in the same range.

decision_rule.support_H_territory: Both bootstrap intervals for zeta_R lie within [1.9, 2.1].

limitations: Polygon generalization at 10 ha affects small lakes; the fixed range mitigates but does not remove it.
Reservoirs are included in HydroLAKES; a sensitivity excluding them (Lake_type != 1) is reported.

amendments.change: Replace the estimator range: select lakes directly on radius of gyration, 1 km <= R <= 20 km, and fit the bounded power law on that fixed interval. Supersedes the area-range selection (1-1000 km^2) with quantile R bounds.
amendments.reason: Synthetic validation of experiments/run_lake_gyration.py showed that selecting on area and then bounding R by quantiles of the selected set biases the fitted zeta_R strongly downwards (true 2.0 estimated as 1.43), because scatter of area at given R depletes the smallest radii, where most lakes lie. Selecting on R itself recovers the truth (2.00 [1.97, 2.03]; a true 2.3 is correctly rejected). R >= 1 km is far above the 10 ha mapping limit (R about 0.2 km); R <= 20 km excludes the few largest lakes.
amendments.unchanged: Hypotheses, data source, projection, bootstrap, decision rule and equivalence margin.
